chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the visitor visits the host and eats with him, he should cast off modesty from himself; and when he eats with him, he should take a little.'
ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for a guest when eating with their host according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explaining the delicate balance of hospitality etiquette: the guest should overcome excessive shyness (hishmah) to allow the host to express generosity, yet eat modestly to avoid becoming a burden. This dual instruction reflects the Shia emphasis on mutual respect and consideration within social bonds, ensuring that hospitality remains a source of joy rather than strain for both parties.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Umar Bin Abdul Aziz, from Jameel Bin Darraj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying that the visitor when he visits the visited, so he eats with him, he should cast off the modesty from him, and when he eats with him, he should take a little’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-’Aziz from Jamil ibn Darraj who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
When a visitor visits someone and eats with him, formality comes down, and when he eats with him (the visitor) feels constraint a little.’”
